title: Functions [The Basics]
description:
## Functions
Functions are just repeatable blocks of code - main is a function, so you've been using one the whole time!
## Defining a function
To define a function, you use the following syntax:
```
<return_type> <name>([argument list]) {
    // code
}
```
I'll explain return_type later. Just ignore it for now. Arguments are what is passed to the function, so let's say you have a function you want to take 2 strings - a and b, then the argument list would be this: `string a, string b`
Arguments are basically variables that are defined when you call a function then disapear after the function ends.
## Returning
Anything inside a function can't be used outside it. To send a value outside a function, you use somthing called a `return` statement. You just type `return <expression>` and that value is sent out. That is what your return type is: the type of the value you return. There is a special return type for a return-less function, `void`. A function _signature_ is what the function definition looks like, so if we have a function that takes a int and a string and returns a float called wierd, its signature would be `float wierd(int a, string b)`.
## Calling a function
Calling a function means to run the code in a function. You call a function with the syntax `<funcname>(<args>);`, and to get the value returned, you would use `<vardecl> = <function call>`.
## Test harnesses
To test that your function works, most function lessons will use somthing called _test harnesses_. The run harness runs when you run your code _not submit_, and it simulates local tests you may have before shipping, and the submit harness runs when you submit your code, and will run more edge cases, like how shipping your code to users would be like. _If the sarter code lacks a main function: **Don't Write It**: It is provided by the test harness._
